Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write a monthly engineering update for a team of twelve, covering a migration, two hires, and a slipped deadline. Around 200 words.

# Engineering update — August

The Postgres 12 to 16 migration finished on the 21st. We ran both clusters in parallel for nine days, cut reads over first, then writes. Two rollbacks during the read phase, both from a connection pooler config we had not tested under load. No data loss, no customer-visible downtime beyond a 40-second write pause at cutover.

Priya Raman joins on the 8th as a backend engineer, coming from the payments team at Wexler. Tom Achebe starts the 22nd on infrastructure. That takes us to twelve. Onboarding buddies are Dani for Priya and Marcus for Tom. If you own a service either of them will touch, expect a walkthrough request in their first fortnight.

The search reindex pipeline slipped. It was due the 29th; it will land mid-September. The cause is on me: I scoped it against the old document schema and did not account for the migration freeze on write-path changes, which cost us two weeks of pipeline work we could not start. Nothing downstream of it is blocked except the relevance A/B test, which moves to October.

September: reindex pipeline, decommission the old cluster, and the on-call rotation rewrite Dani has been drafting.

The deadline slipped again. Update it and explain why.

# Engineering update — September

The search reindex pipeline has slipped again. Mid-September became the 9th of October at the earliest, and I am not going to defend that date hard until we have the schema work landed.

Two causes. The first is real work we did not know about: the new document schema stores facets as a nested JSONB column, and the old indexer flattened them on write. Rebuilding that flattening step inside the pipeline is about eight days of work Marcus scoped last week. The second is that I pulled Priya and Tom onto the old cluster decommission when the storage bill came in higher than forecast, which was the right call for the month and the wrong call for this deadline. I made both calls; the second one I would make again.

The relevance A/B test moves from October to November. Nothing else is downstream.

What I am changing: no more dates on the reindex pipeline until Marcus has written the facet-flattening step and run it against a full corpus snapshot. I would rather tell you nothing for three weeks than move this a third time.

October: facet flattening, cluster decommission finishes on the 6th, and the on-call rotation rewrite goes live on the 13th.
